author: derekchiang
content: as i understand it (<@543900561460822016> can correct me if im wrong), without a PROOF frame or equivalent, wallets would have to validate leanSPHINCS signatures through VERIFY frames, but VERIFY frames are stateful (STATICCALL) so they cannot be aggregated, whereas PROOF frames execute in a pure context (which is why they are a different frame type) so they can be aggregated.  so if we ship H* without PROOF frame (or equivalent), wallets would need to use leanSPHINCS through VERIFY frames, so when aggregation is shipped they will have to update their code (including the smart account code) to leverage aggregation.  so the value of shipping PROOF frames in H* is to be forward-compatible with aggregation so that wallets can transparently take advantage of the cost savings from aggregation once it ships, as opposed to having to update their wallet/account code again

author: derekchiang
content:
what's less clear to me is whether it's feasible to ship aggregation itself in H*.  my understanding is that:

- to support aggregation at the builder level, the primary blocker is the readiness of leanVM itself.  if we are 100% sure that leanVM is production-ready, the remaining questions would be things like figuring out where to put the recursive proof (https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12549).  so it might be doable to resolve these questions in time for H*?

- to support aggregation at the mempool level, besides the readiness of leanVM and other questions we have to resolve for builder aggregation, we also have a lot of networking/mempool questions to answer, such as the exact aggregation strategy that each mempool node is supposed to take (i've done some sims that showed that the strategy currently in the 8288 spec is far from optimal).  not so sure whether it's feasible to resolve these questions by H*, by like <@427491045308235776> said above, we don't actually have to -- as long as the protocol itself can deal with aggregated proofs, we can ship mempool aggregation outside of fork schedule

so my first question (and i guess that's for <@1481393192950567003> <@427491045308235776> <@750602516613431366>) is -- just how production-ready is leanVM for the purpose of aggregating leanSPHINCS signatures as of today?
